Hi Olivia / BrightByte SRE,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get the onboarding benchmarks completed so you can move into production. Attached is a short load spec (brightbyte-load-specs.xlsx) and a Redwood benchmark report template we’ll use to capture results.

High-level plan:
- Week 1 (Jan 18–22): baseline functional runs (single-client latency / safety) and small-scale throughput tests.
- Week 2 (Jan 25–29): multi-client throughput at target QPS, KV cache warmup profiling, and 99th/95th latency sweeps.
- Goal: acceptance gates defined below; if met we schedule production cutover the week of Feb 1.

Acceptance gates (proposed):
- P50 text-gen latency <= 120 ms at 1-token step under steady-state for single-client baseline.
- P95 latency <= 420 ms at your 2-3s average response lengths during 80th percentile traffic.
- Sustained throughput: >= 4000 tokens/sec aggregate across the dedicated pool with <1% error rate.
- No memory spikes above 85% GPU utilization for longer than 30s during 10-minute stress windows.

Requested from BrightByte for Week 1: production-like prompt set (10–20 prompts), representative concurrency profile, and preferred test windows. I’ve copied Marissa (CSM) and Connor (Infra) for coordination on test execution and results capture.

Next step: Olivia — can you confirm the prompt set and give 2 preferred 3-hour windows next week?

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Connor / Vivek — ran the ramp this morning. Initial observations:
- Baseline P50 single-client latency averaged 110 ms (passes P50 gate).
- P95 observed at peak concurrency was 390 ms — within proposed gate.
- Tokens/sec peaked at ~4,200 aggregate; sustained window showed 3,800 tokens/sec at 90% of run.
- GPU util spiked to 88% during one short 20s burst; we captured logs and stack traces (attached).
- Observed 0.6% transient 5xx errors during a backend retry window — investigation ongoing (likely transient infra routing).

Our asks before acceptance:
1) Can Redwood add an additional 15-minute steady-state run at 120% target tomorrow to validate thermal behavior?
2) We’d like a short post-test run with prefix caching disabled to observe cold-start latency profile.

We’ve uploaded RBX-BB-01-logs.tar.gz and a filled-benchmark-report.xlsx to the Drive folder (links in shared Drive notification).
